newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Merrill sees good prospects for greater China.
newsitem.headline: Merrill sees good prospects for greater China.

text.p: Hong Kong's handover to Beijing, expectations of better China-Taiwan relations and an overhaul of the mainland's ailing state sector combine to paint a promising picture for greater China, Merrill Lynch says.

"Greater China will look great in 1997, we believe. Not only is the region well on track for a cyclical rebound, it also seems well set for a landmark structural rebound," Merrill said in a monthly report dated January 17.
The investment house said it expected to see "decisive surgery on China's state sector" in 1997.

A Communist Party congress scheduled for later this year could give Beijing the political opportunity it needs for more aggressive reform, and the economy should be better prepared for an overhaul of its state sector, it said.
Hong Kong will benefit from integration with China after the July 1 transition, the report said, as it "expands its economic periphery beyond southern China".
However, "Hong Kong needs better infrastructure access and improved administration coordination with its hinterland", it said.

On Taiwan, Merrill expects that Hong Kong's handover and pressures over the World Trade Organisation (WTO), which both Beijing and Taipei want to join, could encourage a breakthrough in cross-strait commercial links.
"Immediate benefits of direct links may be limited, but their long-term impacts can hardly be overestimated," the report said.
The greatest risk came from higher U.S. interest rates and weak external demand, it said, but added that any increase in Federal Reserve fund rates would stay within 25-50 basis points over the year.
